cards.explanation: The answer is six, friends. Ezekiel sees six men coming from the Upper Gate, which faces north, and each one has a weapon of slaughter in his hand (Ezekiel 9:2). Six men, six weapons, and a scene this heavy. I'm keeping my apron straight.

The answer is a writing kit, friends. The man clothed in linen has it at his side, and he walks in with the six men who carry weapons (Ezekiel 9:2). Six weapons and one writing kit. I'd be checking my pockets for a pen right about now.

The answer is the men groaning over the abominations. The LORD says to put a mark on the foreheads of the men "…sighing and groaning over all the abominations committed there." (Ezekiel 9:4). The mark goes on the ones who are grieved by what's happening in the city. I think that's one of the most tender details in a very heavy passage.

The answer is False. The LORD tells the six, "do not show pity or spare anyone!" (Ezekiel 9:5). Nothing in that verse mentions anyone begging, and no pity is allowed. It's a heavy line, friends, but it's what the text says.

The answer is anyone who has the mark. The LORD says, "…do not go near anyone who has the mark." (Ezekiel 9:6). That's why the man in linen went first with his writing kit. The mark settles who the six don't touch.

The answer is sanctuary, friends. God says, "Now begin at My sanctuary." and they begin with the elders who were before the temple (Ezekiel 9:6). It's a hard place to start, and the text doesn't give us God's reason. I think that's worth a quiet moment.

Ezekiel asks if God will destroy everyone left in Israel. He falls facedown and cries out, "Oh, Lord GOD, when You pour out Your wrath on Jerusalem, will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?" (Ezekiel 9:8). He's left alone while the killing goes on. I think you can hear how heavy that is in his voice.

The answer is forsaken, friends. God says the people claim, "The LORD has forsaken the land; the LORD does not see." (Ezekiel 9:9). Those are their words, not His. The verse puts them right beside the bloodshed and perversity God names.
The answer is their deeds. God says, "I will bring their deeds down upon their own heads." (Ezekiel 9:10). The word "own" is in the verse, friends. What comes back on them is what they did.

The answer is True. The man clothed in linen with the writing kit at his side reports back, "I have done as You commanded." (Ezekiel 9:11). That's the last line of the passage, friends, and it's short and plain. He was sent to do something and he reports that it's done.
